newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DON'S HAMMAM STILL IN CONTROL DESPITE NORWEGIAN DEAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DON'S HAMMAM STILL IN CONTROL DESPITE NORWEGIAN DEAL.

text.p: Wimbledon boss Sam Hammam insisted he would remain in charge of the English premier league club despite Wednesday's news of a deal to sell a majority stake to two Norwegian millionaires.

The charismatic owner and managing director of the southwest London club, said the arrangement with entrepreneurs Kjell Inge Roekke and Bjoern Rune Gjelsten was not a buy-out and he would continue to run Wimbledon on a day-to-day basis.
"I'm not selling out...I will be in complete charge of all the key decisions of the club," Hammam told local television.
"I am the steering wheel. My foot is on the accelerator and my foot is on the brake."

Hammam stressed that the deal, which the NTB news agency in Norway said amounted to an 80 percent stake worth 300 million crowns ($42 million), would not result in the Dons spending huge sums on new players or increasing wages.
"All we have at this point in time is an engagement to get married and it will be at least a few months before the marriage is consummated.
"I will be delighted to call them my partners in the future but we are not looking at them as sugar daddies," Hammam told a news conference at the club's training ground in south London.
The Norwegian business partners are also major shareholders in Norwegian elite division club Molde.
Roekke, who divides his time between London and Oslo, is expected to play an active role in the running of the club, said NTB.
Gjelsten is based in the Norwegian capital where he is chief executive officer of Norwegian holding company Aker RGI ASA, of which Roekke is the major shareholder.
Wimbledon share the Selhurst Park ground with Crystal Palace. The team finished eighth in the premier division last season.
